clue.text: Captured by old foe, rich industrialists' heads roll

indicators.note: the heads of the industrialists are held inside the old enemy, so this signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: Boche is an old derogatory term for a German, Britain's foe in the world wars

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Wealthy industrialists taken by an ancient enemy face execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like part of the execution picture ('heads roll') but it is the definition, a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a rich, sweet French bread, often baked as a small individual bun.

clue.text: Scottish island is a smasher, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that a word spoken aloud gives the entry's sound

parts.note: a beaut is informal for a smasher, something excellent

explanation.surface: A Scottish isle is said to be a real stunner.
explanation.walkthrough: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde; BEAUT (a beauty, a smasher) is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Bute is an island off the west coast of Scotland, in the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: See 15
Hawthorn's first in flower — the first in the field

indicators.note: in places the initial of Hawthorn within the flower's name

parts.note: the campion is a wild flower of the pink family

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Hawthorn is used

explanation.surface: A horticultural show where the hawthorn entry leads among the blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's second 'first' is part of the definition: whoever comes first in a field of competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the winner, the one placed top among all the competitors in a contest.

clue.text: Extension to accommodate governor or foreign resident

indicators.note: to accommodate means the abbreviation for extension houses the other piece inside it

parts.note: EXT is the usual abbreviation for extension, as on a phone number
governor is old slang for one's father, so PA

explanation.surface: Building an extension to house a governor or someone from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat is an expatriate, someone living outside their native country.

clue.text: Crazy plan to restrain military assistant

indicators.note: to restrain means the plan holds the assistant inside it

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart of an area
ADC stands for aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a senior commander

explanation.surface: A mad scheme to hold back an officer's aide.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap is an adjective meaning recklessly wild or eccentric, a synonym of crazy.

clue.text: A demon barber's disagreeing

parts.note: Sweeney Todd is the demon barber of Fleet Street, so TODD plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A villainous hairdresser's establishment, described in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd, the 'demon barber of Fleet Street', is a Victorian penny-dreadful villain made famous by stage and musical versions.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at odds is an idiom for being in conflict or disagreement with someone.

clue.text: What actors do in preparation for "Privates on Parade"?

definitions.text: What actors do in preparation for "Privates on Parade"?

parts.words: What actors do in preparation for "Privates on Parade"?
parts.note: actors con (learn by heart) their scripts before a play; read as one word, that gives a name for privates, soldiers called up to serve

explanation.surface: Actors rehearsing lines for a production of Peter Nichols's army comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'con' is an old verb meaning to study or learn; Privates on Parade is a British stage comedy about an army concert party.
explanation.definitionFit: Privates who are drafted into military service rather than volunteering are called by this name.

clue.text: Agreeable remark made by learner in class

indicators.note: in means the learner's letter goes inside the word for the class

parts.note: the peasantry is a social class of farm labourers
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A nice comment from a student in a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' suggests a school lesson, following 'learner'; it is the social class.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a polite, friendly or jocular remark made in conversation.

clue.text: 17, having left actors touring Western Australia in Greek comedy

indicators.note: touring means the shortened word for actors travels round the state's abbreviation, enclosing it
having left means that clue 17's answer departs from the word for actors

parts.note: thespians is a word for actors
this refers to the answer to 17 across, McKellen's first name
WA is the standard abbreviation for the state of Western Australia

explanation.surface: Actors on a tour of Western Australia staging a classical comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having left' takes the three letters out of the word for actors, leaving THESPS; 'touring' wraps that round the state. The Greek comedy is by Aristophanes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a comedy by Aristophanes, first staged in Athens in 422 BC.

clue.text: Bump start for Jellicle Cat

indicators.note: start for means only the opening letter of Jellicle is taken

parts.note: the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: Bumping a song from the musical Cats about Jellicle cats.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellicle cats come from T. S. Eliot's poems and the musical Cats, but here 'Cat' is the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: To jounce is to jolt or bounce up and down, as in a bumpy ride.

clue.text: See overleaf, letter revealing author …

indicators.note: over, as in knocked over, signals that the letters of leaf are turned about into a new order

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A note sends the reader to the following page, where a letter discloses the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See overleaf' and the ellipsis point to the next clue, 13 down, written by this author. 'Over' rearranges LEAF into LEFA; 'See' and 'revealing' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan Le Fanu was a nineteenth-century Irish writer of Gothic and mystery fiction.

clue.text: Puddings detected by detectives …

parts.note: spotted means noticed or detected
dicks is slang for private detectives

explanation.surface: Desserts uncovered by police investigators.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding studded with currants or raisins.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted dick is a traditional British steamed sponge pudding made with suet and dried fruit.

clue.text: … left out distressing seal culls in novel

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is taken away from the pool of letters
distressing suggests the letters are upset and jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Upsetting seal culls feature in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: SEALCULLSIN has eleven letters; once one L is taken out, the rest rearrange into the answer. The ellipsis joins it to 11 down, its author.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1864 Gothic mystery novel was written by Sheridan Le Fanu.

clue.text: Is delighted with Proms broadcasting?

parts.note: a prom, short for promenade, is a walk, so the plural gives walks
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: Thrilled because the BBC Proms concerts are being transmitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are an annual series of BBC classical concerts in London; 'prom' also means a walk, a promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on air is an idiom meaning to feel elated or extremely happy.

clue.text: … multicoloured sweets (see in an optical illusion)

indicators.note: an illusion deceives the eye, so the letters are shown in a deceptive new arrangement

explanation.surface: Treats in many colours that trick the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis just continues the run of linked clues; the parenthesis holds the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitan ice cream comes in layered bands of different colours and flavours.

clue.text: Round number that is least productive

indicators.note: Round means that the Latin phrase surrounds the numeral, holding it within

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated ie
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Asking which numerical round was the least productive.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlest is the superlative of idle, meaning doing the least work or producing least.

clue.text: McKellen possibly in a play

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are moved about freely, rearranged

explanation.surface: The actor Sir Ian McKellen perhaps appearing on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the definition as one example of a man with this first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Ian McKellen is a famous English actor, so this forename fits him as an example.

clue.text: Produce withered auricula

parts.note: to bear is to produce, as a tree bears fruit
sear, also spelt sere, means dried up or withered

explanation.surface: Growing a shrivelled primula.
explanation.definitionFit: The auricula is a primula once called this from the shape of its leaves.

clue.text: Table knives slice dough for Albanians

indicators.note: slice suggests cutting a piece out of the words Table knives, which holds the letters

explanation.surface: Cutlery is used to cut up bread dough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like bread to be sliced; it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The lek is the currency of Albania, and dough is slang for money.

clue.text: Cheese for Clarence's brother

definitions.meaning: Double or Single ... is an English hard cheese
Richard, Duke of this county, was brother of George, Duke of Clarence, in Shakespeare's history plays

explanation.walkthrough: Gloucester is an English county; in Richard III, Richard, Duke of Gloucester, has his brother Clarence murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: This county name is both a cheese and the dukedom of Richard III before he was king.

clue.text: An Arabian craft? Very much so!

parts.note: a dhow is a sailing boat used around the Arabian Sea

explanation.surface: Is that an Arab sailing vessel? Absolutely!
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic exclamation of agreement, meaning very much indeed, as in yes, certainly.

clue.text: In London reason equals madness

indicators.note: madness suggests the letters are crazily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A London claim that being sensible amounts to insanity.
explanation.walkthrough: Sloane Square is a square and Tube station in Chelsea, London; the definition is just where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloane Square is a well-known square in Chelsea, a place found within the capital.

clue.text: Open country — more for musicians to get upset about

indicators.note: about means the turned musical word goes around the country's letters
to get upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: piu is Italian for more, used in musical directions such as piu mosso
NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand

explanation.surface: A country where musicians are upset by something extra.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to get upset' means turned upside down, giving UIP; 'about' then wraps that round the country's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To unzip is to open something by undoing its zip fastener.

clue.text: Prevent attendant causing obstruction

parts.note: to stop is to prevent
a page is a young attendant or servant

explanation.surface: Stopping a servant from causing a blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a blockage, as of a pipe, or a halting of work.

clue.text: See 24
See "hate awfully"!

parts.note: lo is an old interjection meaning look or see

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of hate are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dictionary cross-reference directing the reader to a strong phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: to hate awfully is just what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest, to feel intense disgust or hatred towards something.

clue.text: News for Russians from samizdat centre: revolting natives deposed leader

indicators.note: centre means the middle letters of samizdat are taken
revolting suggests the letters rise up and are turned into a new order
deposed leader means the first letter of natives is removed

explanation.surface: A Soviet dissident underground press reports a native uprising that toppled the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposed leader' drops the first letter of natives, leaving ATIVES; 'revolting' rearranges those six letters into VESTIA. Samizdat was the Soviet underground press, fitting the Russian theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Izvestia, meaning 'news' in Russian, was the official newspaper of the Soviet government.

clue.text: Eccentric prison officer's an unknown quantity

parts.note: screw is British slang for a prison officer
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns; here Y

explanation.surface: An odd jailer remains an unknown quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwy is informal for odd, crazy or eccentric.

clue.text: Hat that may be eaten

definitions.meaning: a flat-crowned hat with a brim turned up all round, named for its shape
a savoury pastry filled with chopped pork, eaten cold

explanation.walkthrough: A pork pie is a British meat pie with hot-water pastry; the hat is named after its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one name: a flat-topped hat and a raised pastry with a meat filling.
